item.title: Affordable Housing
item.description:
Affordable housing programs and data.

Plans and Data#

  • ABC Comprehensive Plan, Chapter 9: Housing (2025 Update)

    The housing element of the adopted Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Comprehensive Plan sets policies for housing choice, affordability, neighborhood stability, fair housing, infrastructure, and coordinated implementation across the city and unincorporated county.

  • Albuquerque Region Housing Needs Assessment (2024)

    Prepared for the City of Albuquerque and Mid-Region Council of Governments, this regional assessment documents current housing needs, production needs, vacant-land capacity, growth, fair-share analysis, demographic trends, and conditions affecting housing affordability across the Albuquerque region.

item.title: Development Process
item.description:
Cross-cutting development process documents, manuals, and reference materials.

Development Process Manual#

  • Development Process Manual (June 2, 2020)
    • Provides the City’s technical requirements and procedures for planning, designing, reviewing, permitting, and constructing public infrastructure associated with development projects.

item.title: Homeless Services
item.description:
Homeless services and shelter data.

Current resources and transparency#

  • Emergency shelters, day shelters, and street outreach

    The City maintains this service directory for emergency overnight shelter, day shelter, and street-outreach options. Availability and intake requirements can change; the page directs people needing help to call 311 or the relevant provider.

  • Shelter resources and encampment transparency

    This City page links current shelter-resource information, the Shelter Connect dashboard, and publicly reported encampment-response data. Reported locations are not a substitute for on-the-ground verification.

item.title: Housing Pipeline
item.description:
Current and planned housing development projects.

Uptown Connect#

  • Uptown Connect project page

    Documents the mixed-use redevelopment planned at the Uptown Transit Center, including affordable and market-rate housing, commercial space, transit access, project stages, renderings, and the anticipated 2026–2028 construction schedule.

Development activity data#

  • Building permits open data

    The City’s maintained building-permit data is the most useful general-purpose source for recent development activity. A permit is not the same as a completed home, occupancy, affordability commitment, or project delivery date.

item.title: Zoning & IDO
item.description:
Zoning regulations and Integrated Development Ordinance information.

Current ordinance and zoning tools#

  • Integrated Development Ordinance — effective May 6, 2026

    The City’s current Integrated Development Ordinance establishes zoning, development standards, and review procedures for Albuquerque. This preserved original is the effective May 2026 release; the City IDO page retains archived updates and legislative history.

  • Interactive IDO zoning map

    Search an address or parcel and inspect the mapped zoning layer. Map results should be checked against the effective IDO and City review staff for a site-specific determination.
